body.en: Derivatives reveal where a function rises, falls and curves, and pin down its maxima and minima.
The Mean Value Theorem made visible: the amber secant joins the endpoints, and somewhere between them a tangent (dashed) runs exactly parallel. Slide the right endpoint \( b \).

caption.en: Sampled points on the curve between the secant's endpoints

note.en: There is a \( c \) in \( (a,b) \) with \( f'(c)=\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \) — the ringed point.

body.en: Mean Value Theorem: some \( c \) has \( f'(c)=\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \). \( f \) increases where \( f'>0 \) and is concave up where \( f''>0 \). The first- and second-derivative tests classify critical points; optimization finds extreme values.

figure.title: Curve Analysis: Extrema and Inflection Point

caption.en: On $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2$, $f'(x) = 3x(x-2) = 0$ identifies critical points at $x=0$ and $x=2$. The second derivative $f''(x) = 6x - 6$ changes from negative (concave down) to positive (concave up) at the inflection point $(1,-2)$.

body.en:
Classify the critical points of \( f(x)=x^{3}-3x^{2} \).

\( f'(x)=3x^{2}-6x=3x(x-2) \), so \( x=0,2 \). With \( f''(x)=6x-6 \): \( f''(0)<0 \), \( f''(2)>0 \).

\[ \text{Local max at }x=0,\quad \text{local min at }x=2. \]

A farmer has 200 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular field with one side along a river (no fence needed there). What dimensions maximise the area?

Let width \(=x\), length \(=y\). Constraint: \(2x+y=200\Rightarrow y=200-2x\).

\[A=xy=x(200-2x)=200x-2x^2.\]\[A'=200-4x=0\;\Rightarrow\;x=50\text{ m},\;y=100\text{ m}.\quad A_{\max}=5000\text{ m}^2.\]

label.en: ⚠ Common traps — FRQ justification language & inflection points

body.en:
Strict AP justification phrasing: State “\( f \) has a local minimum at \( x = 2 \) because \( f'(x) \) changes from negative to positive at \( x = 2 \)”. Never write “the graph turns around” or “it changes sign” without specifying \( f' \). Referring to an unnamed “it” forfeits justification points.

\( f''(c) = 0 \) alone is NOT an inflection point: An inflection point requires an actual change in concavity (i.e. \( f''(x) \) must change sign across \( c \)). For example, \( f(x) = x^4 \) has \( f''(0) = 0 \), but \( f''(x) \ge 0 \) everywhere, so there is no inflection point.

Candidates Test for absolute extrema: On a closed interval \( [a, b] \), absolute extrema can occur at critical points OR at endpoints. You must construct a table evaluating \( f(x) \) at \( x = a \), \( x = b \), and all interior critical points.

question.en: Verify the Mean Value Theorem for \(f(x)=x^3\) on \([0,2]\) by finding the value \(c\).
